lemma: Pol(R) for R={100,010,001} over {0,1} consists exactly of the projections, in every arity k>=1.
proved_step: Let f:{0,1}^k->{0,1} preserve R; put g(S)=f(1_S) for S subset [k]. For any sigma:[k]->{1,2,3} the k input tuples e_sigma(j) lie in R, and the output column c is 1_{sigma^-1(c)}; so for every ordered partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks exactly one of g(B1),g(B2),g(B3) equals 1. (a) (empty,empty,[k]) gives g(empty)=0, g([k])=1. (b) (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1. (c) for disjoint S,T with U=(S u T)^c, (S,T,U) gives g(S)+g(T)+g(U)=1 and by (b) g(U)=1-g(S u T), so g(S u T)=g(S)+g(T). (d) Induction from (a),(c): g(S)=sum_{i in S} g({i}); since g([k])=1 and values are 0/1, exactly one i has g({i})=1, so g(S)=[i in S] and f=x_i. Converse: projections preserve R. Hence Pol(R)=projections. Scope: general k, proof written, exact check pending for k<=6 (see physalis_code_run).

lemma: For every k>=1 and every f:{0,1}^k->{0,1}: f preserves R={100,010,001} (as a 3-ary relation) iff, for every ordered partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks, exactly one of f(1_B1), f(1_B2), f(1_B3) equals 1. Consequently every such polymorphism is a projection x_i.
evidence: PROOF. (a) Columns of three rows of R are unit vectors e_b, so applying f coordinatewise to three rows of R gives x^(j)_i = [b(i)=j] = 1_{Bj}(i) for a function b:[k]->{1,2,3}; the output is in R iff exactly one of f(1_B1),f(1_B2),f(1_B3) is 1. (b) g(S):=f(1_S). Taking (B1,B2,B3)=(∅,∅,[k]) gives g(∅)=0 (two equal values cannot give exactly one 1), and g([k])=1. Taking (S,S^c,∅) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1. For disjoint S,T with U=(S∪T)^c, exactly one of g(S),g(T),g(U) is 1, so g(S∪T)=1-g(U)=g(S)+g(T). (c) Additivity over disjoint unions with values in {0,1} gives g(S)=sum_{i in S} g({i}); g([k])=1 forces exactly one i with g({i})=1, so g(S)=[i in S]. Every x in {0,1}^k is 1_S for S={i: x_i=1}, hence f(x)=x_i. Converse (projections preserve R) is immediate. Works for all k>=1, so the k<=6 check is a special case. FINITE CHECK: physalis code cm-33883e2c2acb4072 (exhaustive SAT/enumeration, k=1..6): exactly k polymorphisms, all projections. STATUS: proof is hand-verified by the proving session only; it is CLAIMED until a different session reviews it. The validator claim claim:fcb651188287 is still PENDING. lemma: Constants are pp-definable from R={100,010,001} with equality. phi1(x) := exists y,z [R(x,y,z) and y=z] defines {1}. phi0(x) := exists z [phi1(z) and R(x,x,z)] defines {0}. Hence, with Pol(R)=projections (S0001), Geiger/BKKR gives that every Boolean relation is pp-definable from {R} plus equality, with no constants needed.
evidence: PROOF. Tuples of R with y=z: only (1,0,0), so R(x,y,y) forces x=1 and y=0; phi1 = {1}. Tuples of R with x=y: only (0,0,1), so R(x,x,z) forces x=0 and z=1; with phi1(z) (z=1) this gives phi0 = {0}. Galois connection (Geiger 1968, Bodnarchuk-Kaluzhnin-Kotov-Romov 1969): a relation is pp-definable from Gamma (with equality and constants) iff Pol(Gamma) preserves it. Pol(R)=projections preserves every relation, so every Boolean relation is pp-definable from R. STATUS: CLAIMED; the pp-definitions are checkable by a finite enumeration (2^3 cases each). Not yet verified: (ii) the F_3-linear to positive 1-in-3 FO reduction, and (iii) the Atserias-Bulatov-Dawar / Anderson-Dawar corollary.

lemma: For every arity k>=1, every k-ary polymorphism of R={100,010,001} is a projection, i.e. Pol(R) = {x_1,...,x_k}. Proof uses only the exactly-one property of R under coordinatewise application.
proved_step: Let f:{0,1}^k->{0,1} preserve R (applying f coordinatewise to k tuples of R yields a tuple of R). Set g(S)=f(1_S) for S subset [k]. (1) Give tuple j the 1 in row p_j in {1,2,3}; output row i is g(S_i) with S_i={j: p_j=i}. Hence for every ordered partition (S1,S2,S3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks, exactly one of g(S1),g(S2),g(S3) equals 1. (2) Partition (empty,empty,[k]) gives g(empty)=0 and g([k])=1. Partition (empty,S,[k]\S) gives g(S)+g([k]\S)=1. (3) F={S: g(S)=1} is nonempty and has no two disjoint members (partition (A,B,rest) would have two 1s). Let M be inclusion-minimal in F; M is nonempty since g(empty)=0. If |M|>=2, pick a in M and use the partition ({a}, M\{a}, [k]\M): g(M\{a})=0 by minimality, g([k]\M)=1-g(M)=0, so g({a})=1, contradicting minimality. So M={i}. (4) Every B in F meets {i} (no disjoint members), so i in B; if i in S then [k]\S not in F, so S in F. Hence g(S)=[i in S] and f is the projection onto coordinate i. Projections trivially preserve R. Hypothesis checked: only the exactly-one-per-3-partition property; this is a clone fact, not a circuit bound, so no barrier applies. Status: CLAIMED until a different session reviews it. NOT covered: the pp-definability consequence (Geiger/BKKR), the F_3-linear-equations reduction item, and the source check of Geiger/BKKR.

proved_step: CONTROL LEMMA (arity k>=1). Let f:{0,1}^k->{0,1} preserve R={100,010,001}, i.e. for any k tuples r^1..r^k in R, (f(row1),f(row2),f(row3)) in R, where row_l = (r^1_l,...,r^k_l). For S subset [k] put g(S)=f(1_S). Proof: (1) For the 3-partition (P1,P2,P3) of [k] (blocks may be empty), column j = unit vector e_l with j in P_l, so each column lies in R and (g(P1),g(P2),g(P3)) in R: exactly one block has g=1. (2) Partition ([k],empty,empty) gives g(empty)=0 (else two ones). (3) Partition (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1. (4) F={S: g(S)=1} is nonempty (g([k])=1) and intersecting (disjoint T1,T2 in F contradict (1) with the third block). (5) Let T in F be minimal (T nonempty since g(empty)=0). If |T|>=2, split T=T1 disjoint-union T2 with both nonempty; neither is in F by minimality, so (1) on (T1,T2,[k]\T) gives [k]\T in F, which is disjoint from T: contradiction. So T={i}. (6) Every member of F meets {i}, so contains i. For S with i not in S: i in S^c, so g(S^c)=1 and by (3) g(S)=0. For i in S: S meets {i}, so g(S)=1. Hence f(x)=x_i on all of {0,1}^k. Projections satisfy the condition, so the polymorphisms are exactly the k projections. Scope: Boolean (2-valued) polymorphisms of R of every arity k>=1. Status: CLAIMED, not yet reviewed by another session. Uses nothing outside the definition of polymorphism.

evidence: Reviewed by an independent session. Steps (1)-(5) re-derived and correct: (1) column j = e_{a_j} gives row-block indicators 1_{P_l}, so (g(P1),g(P2),g(P3)) in R; (2) partition ([k],empty,empty) gives g(empty)=0 and g([k])=1; (3) partition (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1; (4) F intersecting via (T1,T2,rest); (5) minimal T in F is a singleton {i} via (T1,T2,[k]\T). GAP in step (6) as written: 'i in S^c so g(S^c)=1' and 'S meets {i} so g(S)=1' do not follow from the stated facts. REPAIR: for S containing i, if g(S)=0 then g(S^c)=1 by (3), so S^c in F, but i is not in S^c, contradicting that every F-member contains i; hence g(S)=1. For S not containing i, g(S)=1 would put S in F without i, so g(S)=0. Hence f = x_i. Exact check cm-a914f53b40ea4c52 (k=1..4, all 2^(2^k) functions, direct from R): survivors are exactly the k projections. Conclusion of the lemma survives; the write-up needs the repaired step (6).

proved_step: LEMMA (control, all arities; repairs the singleton sub-step of S0019). For every k>=1, every k-ary Boolean polymorphism f of R={100,010,001} is a projection f(x)=x_i. Proof: let g(S)=f(1_S), F={S: g(S)=1}. (a) Coordinatewise application to k tuples e_{p_j} in R gives: for every ordered partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks, exactly one of g(B1),g(B2),g(B3) equals 1. (b) Partition (empty,empty,[k]) gives g([k])=1, g(empty)=0; partition (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S^c)=1-g(S). (c) F is intersecting: disjoint S,T in F would give two blocks with value 1 in (S,T,rest). (d) F contains [k]; let M be a minimal member. If |M|>=2, pick a in M and use the partition ({a}, M\{a}, M^c): {a} and M\{a} are proper subsets of M so not in F; g(M^c)=1-g(M)=0; all three values 0, contradicting (a). So M={i}. (e) Every S in F meets {i} by (c), so i in S. Conversely if i in S and g(S)=0 then g(S^c)=1, so S^c in F with i not in S^c, contradicting (e). Hence g(S)=[i in S], i.e. f=x_i. Scope: Boolean polymorphisms of R, all arities k>=1; Pol(R)=projections. Does not close G0001 (symmetric-majority corollary, item iii) or G0007 (constant-free closure); the idempotent route predicts all 256 relations constant-free, still open.

Galois correspondence is a cited classical theorem (Geiger 1968; BKKR 1969), used in its exact form: Inv(Pol(Gamma)) = relations pp-definable with constants from Gamma. proved_step: Lemma (G0007, constants step): for R={(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)} on {0,1}, (a) the pp-formula exists z: R(x,x,z) defines exactly {x=0}, since the only tuples of R with first two coordinates equal are (0,0,1), forcing x=0, z=1; (b) exists z: R(z,z,x) defines exactly {x=1}, since the only such tuple is (0,0,1), forcing z=0, x=1. Both formulas are constant-free (variable identification and existential quantification only). Hence the unary constant relations {0} and {1} are constant-free pp-definable from R. Combined with S0022 (Pol(R) = projections for every arity), Pol(R, {0}, {1}) is also the set of projections, so by the Geiger / Bodnarchuk-Kaluzhnin-Kotov-Romov Galois correspondence every Boolean relation of every arity is pp-definable from R with constants, and by substitution of the constants above, constant-free. This proves the all-arity form of G0007, superseding the finite arity-3 certificate S0025 (which is kept as a consistency check). Status: CLAIMED; not reviewed by this session.

Logical verification of the partition argument: (1) f preserves R={100,010,001} means for any k tuples in R, coordinate-wise f gives a tuple in R. (2) For any ordered 3-partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k], construct k input tuples where tuple j is the unit vector e_l with l being the block containing j. Each input tuple is in R. The i-th output bit is f applied to the indicator of Bi, i.e., g(Bi). Since output must be in R, exactly one g(Bi)=1. (3) Partition (empty,empty,[k]) gives g(empty)=0, g([k])=1. (4) Partition (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1. (5) For disjoint S,T with U=(S∪T)^c, partition (S,T,U) gives g(S)+g(T)+g(U)=1; with (4), g(U)=1-g(S∪T), so g(S∪T)=g(S)+g(T). (6) By induction g(S)=sum_{i∈S} g({i}); g([k])=1 and 0/1 values force exactly one i with g({i})=1, so g(S)=[i∈S] and f is projection x_i. Converse: projections trivially preserve R. No gap found; proof is correct for all k≥1.

Verified the pp-definitions by exhaustive case analysis on the 3 tuples of R={100,010,001}:
- phi1(x) := exists y,z [R(x,y,z) and y=z]:
  * (1,0,0): y=0,z=0 so y=z holds, x=1 -> phi1(1)=true
  * (0,1,0): y=1,z=0 so y≠z -> false
  * (0,0,1): y=0,z=1 so y≠z -> false
  Thus phi1 defines exactly {1}.
- phi0(x) := exists z [phi1(z) and R(x,x,z)]:
  * phi1(z) forces z=1
  * R(x,x,1): only tuple with third coordinate 1 is (0,0,1)
  * So x=0, x=0, z=1 -> x must be 0
  Thus phi0 defines exactly {0}.
Both definitions are correct over the Boolean domain with existential quantification, conjunction, and equality. No gap found.

Verified the partition argument with minimal-element proof:
1. f preserves R={100,010,001} means for any 3-partition (S1,S2,S3) of [k], exactly one g(Si)=1 where g(S)=f(1_S).
2. (empty,empty,[k]) gives g(empty)=0, g([k])=1.
3. (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1.
4. F={S: g(S)=1} is nonempty (contains [k]) and intersecting (no two disjoint members, else partition would give two 1s).
5. Let M be inclusion-minimal in F; M≠∅ since g(empty)=0.
6. If |M|≥2, pick a∈M. Partition ({a}, M\{a}, [k]\M): g(M\{a})=0 by minimality, g([k]\M)=1-g(M)=0 by (3), so g({a})=1, contradicting minimality. Hence M={i} is a singleton.
7. Every B∈F meets {i} (intersecting), so i∈B. If i∈S and S∉F, then S^c∈F by (3), but i∉S^c contradicts i∈B for all B∈F. If i∉S and S∈F, then i∉S contradicts i∈B for all B∈F. So g(S)=1 iff i∈S, hence f=x_i.
Projections preserve R trivially. Proof is correct for all k≥1. No gap found.

Verified the clean partition proof:
- g(S)=f(1_S), F={S: g(S)=1}. Partition property: any ordered 3-partition has exactly one g=1.
- g(empty)=0, g([k])=1, g(S)+g(S^c)=1 (from partitions (empty,empty,[k]), ([k],empty,empty), (S,S^c,empty)).
- F nonempty, intersecting (disjoint T1,T2 in F would give two 1s in partition (T1,T2,[k]\T1\T2)).
- Let T be minimal in F; T≠∅. If |T|≥2, split T=T1∪T2 disjoint nonempty. By minimality g(T1)=g(T2)=0, so g([k]\T)=1, i.e. [k]\T∈F, disjoint from T: contradiction. So T={i}.
- For S with i∈S: if g(S)=0 then g(S^c)=1 so S^c∈F but i∉S^c, contradicting all F-members contain i (they meet {i}).
- For S with i∉S: S^c contains i so g(S^c)=1, hence g(S)=0.
- Thus f(x)=x_i. Proof is complete, correct for all k≥1, uses only the definition of polymorphism. No gap found.

This step claims the constant-free pp-closure of R={100,010,001} contains all 256 Boolean relations of arity 3, citing a finite certificate computation (cm-94381695be9940b1). However, this is REFUTED by the idempotent polymorphism analysis: Pol(R) = projections (S0022, SURVIVED_REVIEW). The idempotent Galois correspondence states Inv(Pol_id(R)) = constant-free pp-closure of R. Since Pol_id(R) = projections (all projections are idempotent), the invariant is ALL Boolean relations - but this is for the FULL set of projections. However, the constant-free pp-closure of a SINGLE relation R with Pol(R)=projections should be exactly the relations invariant under all projections, which are the DICTATOR relations (essentially unary relations lifted to higher arity). There are far fewer than 256 arity-3 relations invariant under all projections - projections force all coordinates to be equal or a single coordinate to determine the output. A concrete counterexample: the relation {(0,1,0), (1,0,1)} (parity of first two bits) is NOT constant-free pp-definable from R because it's not invariant under the projection to coordinate 1 (which preserves R). The computational certificate likely had a bug or used constants implicitly. The claim that ALL 256 arity-3 relations are generated is false.

Verified the consequence step as a correct application of the classical Galois correspondence:
- S0009 (SURVIVED_REVIEW): Pol(R) = all projections for R={100,010,001}.
- S0011 (SURVIVED_REVIEW): constants 0 and 1 are pp-definable from R (with existential quantifiers and equality).
- Galois correspondence (Geiger 1968; Bodnarchuk-Kaluzhnin-Kotov-Romov 1969): For a finite domain, Inv(Pol(Gamma)) = relations pp-definable from Gamma with equality allowed, constants not required.
- The clone of ALL projections preserves EVERY relation (for any tuples t1..tk in a relation, projection to coordinate i gives ti which is in the relation by assumption). Hence Inv(projections) = all Boolean relations.
- Therefore pp-closure of R with equality = all Boolean relations.
- Adding the pp-definable constants 0 and 1 (S0011) gives pp-closure of R with constants = all Boolean relations.
- The step correctly deduces that all unary and binary Boolean relations are in the pp-closure (a corollary of all relations being in it).
This is a correct theorem application, not a new proof. No gap found.

Verified the partition argument in S0016:
- f preserves R={100,010,001}, g(S)=f(1_S).
- (1) For any 3-partition (P1,P2,P3) of [k], columns are unit vectors in R, so (g(P1),g(P2),g(P3)) in R => exactly one g(Pi)=1.
- (2) Partition ([k],empty,empty) gives g(empty)=0 (else two 1s). Actually, this partition gives (g([k]),g(empty),g(empty)) in R. For this to be in R={100,010,001}, exactly one coordinate is 1. If g([k])=1 then g(empty)=0. If g([k])=0 then both g(empty) would need to be 1 and 0 simultaneously - impossible. So g([k])=1, g(empty)=0.
- (3) Partition (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1 (since exactly one of the three is 1, and g(empty)=0).
- (4) F={S: g(S)=1} nonempty ([k] in F) and intersecting (disjoint T1,T2 in F would give two 1s in partition (T1,T2,rest)).
- (5) Let T in F be minimal; T nonempty. If |T|>=2, split T=T1∪T2 disjoint nonempty. By minimality g(T1)=g(T2)=0, so from partition (T1,T2,[k]\T) we get g([k]\T)=1, so [k]\T in F, disjoint from T: contradiction. So T={i}.
- (6) Every member of F meets {i} (intersecting), so contains i. For S with i∉S: i∈S^c so g(S^c)=1 so g(S)=0. For i∈S: S meets {i} so S∈F so g(S)=1. Hence f(x)=x_i.
Proof is correct and equivalent to S0009/S0022. No gap found.

Verified the repair of step (6) in S0016:
- Given: F={S: g(S)=1} is intersecting, contains [k], has singleton minimal member {i}.
- Claim: g(S)=1 iff i∈S.
- Proof: If i∈S and g(S)=0, then g(S^c)=1 (by g(S)+g(S^c)=1), so S^c∈F but i∉S^c. But every F-member contains i (since all meet {i}), contradiction. If i∉S and g(S)=1, then S∈F but i∉S, contradiction. Hence g(S)=[i∈S] and f(x)=x_i.
- This is a clean completion of the minimal-element argument. Correct for all k≥1. No gap found.

Verified the constant-free pp-definability of {0} and {1} from R:
- R = {(1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1)}.
- (a) ∃z R(x,x,z): tuples with first two coordinates equal: only (0,0,1). So x=0, z=1. Defines {0}.
- (b) ∃z R(z,z,x): tuples with first two coordinates equal: only (0,0,1). So z=0, x=1. Defines {1}.
- Both use only variable identification and existential quantification - constant-free.
- With {0} and {1} constant-free pp-definable, we have constants in the constant-free closure.
- Pol(R) = projections (S0022, SURVIVED_REVIEW). Adding constants doesn't change the clone (projections preserve all constants).
- Galois correspondence with constants: Inv(Pol(R,{0},{1})) = pp-closure of R with constants = all Boolean relations.
- Since {0},{1} are already constant-free pp-definable, substituting them shows every relation is constant-free pp-definable from R.
- This proves the all-arity form of G0007 correctly. The earlier S0025 arity-3 computational claim was refuted (it confused constant-free with constants-allowed closure).
Proof is correct. No gap found.

proved_step: LEMMA (all arities). Let f:{0,1}^k->{0,1} be a polymorphism of R={100,010,001}: applying f coordinatewise to k tuples of R gives a tuple of R. Then f = x_j for some j. PROOF. Put g(S)=f(1_S) for S subset of [k]. For sigma:[k]->[3] the k rows R[sigma(1)],...,R[sigma(k)] have output coordinate i equal to f(1_{sigma^{-1}(i)}). Hence for every ordered partition (B1,B2,B3) of [k] into possibly empty blocks, exactly one Bi has g(Bi)=1 (*). Step 1: (empty,empty,[k]) gives g(empty)=0 and g([k])=1. Step 2: (S,S^c,empty) gives g(S)+g(S^c)=1. Step 3 (upward closed): if g(A)=1 and A subset B, then (A,B\A,B^c) gives g(B^c)=0, and (B,empty,B^c) gives g(B)=1. Step 4 (intersection): let g(A)=g(B)=1, X=A cap B, Y=A\B, Z=B\A. From (X,Y,A^c) and g(A^c)=0: g(X)+g(Y)=1. From (X,Z,B^c) and g(B^c)=0: g(X)+g(Z)=1. If g(X)=0 then g(Y)=g(Z)=1, but (Y,Z,rest) has two members with value 1, contradicting (*). So g(X)=1. Step 5: let M be the intersection of F={S: g(S)=1}; M is in F by Step 4, and M is nonempty since g(empty)=0. If |M|>=2, pick j in M. Then g(M^c)=0 (as M in F), g(M\{j})=0 (minimality of M), so (({j}), M\{j}, M^c) forces g({j})=1, hence M subset {j}, contradiction. So M={j}; Step 3 gives {S: j in S} subset F, and Step 2 gives equality. Thus g(S)=[j in S] and f(x)=x_j. Conversely each projection satisfies (*). QED. Every step is a finite partition check; no arity bound is used.

lemma: STATEMENT: For R={100,010,001} (Boolean, arity 3), every k-ary Boolean polymorphism f of R is a projection, for all k>=1. Hence Inv(Pol(R)) = all Boolean relations, and {010,101} is constant-free pp-definable from R with equality: T(x,y,z) <=> exists w,v: R(x,y,w) and R(w,w,v) and z=x. PROOF: (1) A k-tuple of R-elements is a colouring c:[k]->{1,2,3}; f applied coordinatewise gives output entry i equal to f(1_{A_i}), A_i={j: c(j)=i}. So f preserves R iff for every partition [k]=A_1+A_2+A_3 (empty parts allowed) exactly one of f(1_{A_i}) equals 1. Let F={A: f(1_A)=1}. (2) Partition (empty,empty,[k]) gives f(0)=0 and [k] in F. (3) Partition (A,A^c,empty) gives exactly one of A, A^c in F. (4) No two disjoint members of F (partition (A,B,rest) would give two). (5) F up-closed: if A in F, A subset A', A' not in F, then A'^c in F and is disjoint from A, contradicting (4). (6) F closed under intersection: for A,B in F, A\B and B\A are disjoint from B resp. A so not in F; A^c not in F; partition (A cap B, A\B, A^c) forces A cap B in F. (7) M = intersection of all members of F; M in F by (6), and M nonempty since f(0)=0. If |M|>=2, pick i in M; M\{i} not in F (minimality of M), so its complement is in F; intersecting with M gives {i} in F by (6), so M subset {i}, contradiction. So M={j}; by (5) F={A: j in A}, i.e. f(1_A)=[j in A] for all A, so f is the j-th projection. Checks: brute force arity 1..4 (cm-11ae193d2c8e460a) agrees. The pp-definition is verified by exhaustive enumeration (cm-b2d97f13984041a8). SCOPE: all arities k>=1, Boolean domain, R={100,010,001} exactly. The Galois step uses the standard pp/polymorphism correspondence with equality and no constants (Geiger; Bodnarchuk-Kaluzhnin-Kotov-Romov). STATUS: CLAIMED, needs review by a session of another model family.

lemma: STATEMENT: Over R={100,010,001} (Boolean, arity 3), with equality and no constants, the relations NEQ={(0,1),(1,0)}, {0} and {1} are pp-definable: NEQ(x,y) <=> exists w,v: R(x,y,w) and R(w,w,v); {0}(x) <=> exists z: R(x,x,z); {1}(x) <=> exists z: R(x,z,z). PROOF: (a) R(w,w,v) holds only for (w,v)=(0,1), since R has no tuple with first two coordinates equal to 1 and only (0,0,1) has them equal to 0. (b) So NEQ(x,y) <=> R(x,y,0) <=> (x,y) in {(1,0),(0,1)}, because the tuples of R with third coordinate 0 are 100 and 010. (c) {0}(x) <=> R(x,x,z) for some z: only x=0 works, with z=1 from 001. (d) {1}(x) <=> R(x,z,z) for some z: only x=1 works, with z=0 from 100. Hence the three relations are pp-definable with equality and no constants. Combined with the control lemma (Pol(R) = projections), T={010,101} is pp-definable as the conjunction of NEQ(x,y) with z=x. SCOPE: Boolean domain, R={100,010,001} exactly. EVIDENCE: independent own-encoding check cm-935e492c939b4942 (ALL_OK, predicted equality of all three relations on all inputs; a wrong witness range or coordinate-order error would have produced FAIL). This is an elementary verification, not new mathematics. STATUS: CLAIMED, needs review by another model family.
